alison-streeter-english-channel.paragraph: Streeter swam in both directions in 1992. On 21 September she left France at 13:41 and reached Shakespeare Beach at 00:26 the next day. In New York she raced around Manhattan in 1987, 1999 and 2000, taking fourth place in 1987.

chloe-mccardel-english-channel.paragraph: McCardel crossed from England to France on 4 August 2021 in 9 hours 55 minutes. The CSA awarded her both its fastest solo and fastest women’s swim for that season. Sixteen days later she made her 40th CSA crossing. She had also crossed the Catalina Channel from the island to the California mainland in 2019.

des-renford-english-channel.paragraph: Renford crossed twice within six days in 1975. On 29 July he swam from France to England in 14 hours 22 minutes, with B. Reed on Accord. On 3 August he returned to France in 13 hours 8 minutes, escorted by Reg Brickell Sr on Helen Ann Marie. They were separate solo swims.

mervyn-sharp-english-channel.paragraph: Sharp completed two England-to-France swims in 1969. One took 14 hours 29 minutes and was the outward crossing of an attempted double. The other took 19 hours 41 minutes. His 15-hour-14-minute crossing on 31 July 1970 came eight days before he raced at Windermere.

nora-toledano-cadena-english-channel.paragraph: In 1995 Toledano finished third around Manhattan in 8 hours 9 minutes 8 seconds. She returned in 2001 and finished eighth. In September 2005 she swam from Samphire Hoe to Pointe du Riden in 10 hours 4 minutes, with Michael Oram piloting Gallivant and Laura López Bonilla observing.

shelley-taylor-smith-english-channel.paragraph: Taylor-Smith’s Manhattan swims took her around the island from two starting points. She finished third from Mill Rock in 1984 and first from Pier A at the Battery in 1987. On 14 July 1995 she made the circuit from Mill Rock in 5 hours 45 minutes 25 seconds.

refs.text: Women’s Museum of Australia, Shelley Taylor-Smith

susie-maroney-english-channel.paragraph: After her Manhattan victories in 1990 and 1994, Maroney returned to New York in June 1999. She made the counterclockwise circuit from Pier A at the Battery in 7 hours 15 minutes 59 seconds, placing eighth.

linda-mcgill-english-channel.paragraph: McGill’s three Manhattan results from 1983 to 1986 include swims from Pier A at the Battery and from Mill Rock. Her quickest of the three was 8 hours 23 minutes 10 seconds from Mill Rock in 1984.

antonio-arguelles-english-channel.paragraph: Argüelles swam from Catalina Island to the California mainland in July 1999 and again in October 2008, July 2009 and January 2017. His July 2009 crossing took 10 hours 25 minutes 2 seconds. Five weeks earlier he had finished twelfth around Manhattan.
